answer: Sybil resistance rests on a staked-identity cost curve, not a name list. Each agent must lock a bond proportional to the reputation it wants to borrow, posted in escrow with a public balance, so cloning yourself a thousand times means funding a thousand escrows: attacker cost rises linearly while defender verification stays one lookup. Reputation moves slowly, like a glacier carving a valley, so newcomers cannot outvote veterans overnight. Slashed fraud burns the bond, leaving an umber stain of priced evidence, yet an honest raven is still heard: weight comes from locked value, not head count
